prompt: A shopper buys $s$ shirts costing $\$9$ each and $p$ pairs of pants costing $\$15$ each. She spends no more than $\$120$ and buys at least $4$ shirts. Which system represents this situation?
hint: The sentence contains two separate conditions, one about money and one about shirts. Translate each phrase into its own symbol.

hints.text: The sentence contains two separate conditions, one about money and one about shirts. Translate each phrase into its own symbol.
The cost is $9s + 15p$ because shirts cost $9$ dollars and pants cost $15$ dollars. No more than means $\le$, and at least means $\ge$.
The system is $9s + 15p \le 120$ together with $s \ge 4$, which is choice A.

learningObjective: Translate constraint language into a system of inequalities.
explanation: Total spending is $9s + 15p$, and "no more than $\$120$" allows equality: $9s + 15p \le 120$.
Choice D swaps the prices onto the wrong items; choice C uses strict inequalities, which would wrongly exclude spending exactly $\$120$ or buying exactly $4$ shirts.

alternativeExplanations.title: A translation table worth memorizing
steps: "At least", "no less than", "minimum of" → $\ge$. "At most", "no more than", "maximum of" → $\le$.
The words containing "no" or "at" almost always permit equality; the bare comparison words do not.
